The spec loads, balances, has every link and passes the behaviour checks, so I can report.", "answer": "The spec now loads, its units balance, it contains every link of the hypothesis and it behaves. Changes: Updating perceived wait, units from months to months/month (the equation was right). Overtime, units from extra clinics/month to fraction (the equation was right; the units came from the interview table). Capacity, equation from Normal_capacity + Overtime to Normal_capacity * (1 + Overtime), because a fraction cannot be added to patients/month. Pressure, equation from Perceived_wait / Reference_wait to Waiting_list / Target_list, because the hypothesis has Waiting list -> Pressure and the old rule read the GPs' belief. Target list, added as 32000 patients, the starting list, so the model starts in balance. Waiting time, equation from Waiting_list / Treatments to Waiting_list / MAX(1, Treatments), so a run with no capacity does not divide by zero. Behaviour: the list holds at 32000 until month 12 and rises to 36902 by month 60; with normal_capacity = 0 it rises to 53535; with need_increase = -4000 it falls to 0 with no floor needed. For the modeller to decide: the value of Target list; whether the diagram should show the two links the hypothesis lacks (Waiting list -> Treatments and Treatments -> Waiting time); and a source for the numbers 0.5 and 0.2 in the overtime rule."}

6dd670847c9b74e0.text: The model follows one hospital waiting list, the `Waiting list`, which starts at 32,000 patients. Patients join it as `Referrals` and leave it as `Treatments`, which can never exceed `Capacity`. GPs refer fewer patients when they believe the wait is long; their belief, the `Perceived wait`, catches up with the real wait over a `Perception time` of 6 months, so they react late. Managers watch a `Reported list`, which trails the real list by a `Reporting delay` of 1 month, and when it is above the `Target list` of 32,000 they feel `Pressure` and add `Overtime`. Overtime raises capacity above the `Normal capacity` of 4,000 patients a month, but by no more than the `Maximum overtime` of 0.2, a fifth. In the scenario, `Need in the population` rises by 400 patients a month in month 12, from 4,000 to 4,400. Several of these numbers, including the limit on overtime and how fast managers respond, are assumptions that later chapters test.
